subject: Re: Mid-contract expansion + co-term options for Aurelia Labs
messages:
From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@aurelia.ai>
To: jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Mid-contract expansion: want to add capacity and co-term

Hi Jasmine,

Quick one — we have a product sprint coming up and need to expand our committed capacity mid-term. We're currently on the Standard Reserved tier and would like to add a dedicated pool (approx. 200K reserved units equivalent) and align the new commitment to our existing contract end date (co-term). Procurement also asked whether Redwood can offer accelerated credits to offset immediate uplift costs while we ramp usage.

Can you share: 1) a rough pricing delta for adding the 200K (annualized vs pro-rata), 2) options for co-term annualization vs full-year topup, and 3) whether a one-time accelerator credit is possible to smooth cash flow? Attaching the capacity spec we expect to run.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Ortiz
Head of Platform Engineering, Aurelia Labs
elena.ortiz@aurelia.ai
Attachment: Aurelia_Requested_Specs.pdf (pdf, 178KB)
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@aurelia.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mid-contract expansion: want to add capacity and co-term

Elena — thanks for the note and the spec.

We can absolutely support an incremental dedicated pool and co-term it to your existing renewal date. High-level answers:
- I can run numbers for an annualized uplift vs pro-rata top-up and share a comparison by EOD Monday.
- We typically offer an accelerator credit for mid-contract expansions (one-time credit applied to the first invoice) for customers doing faster ramp. I need to confirm quantum with finance/sales ops.
- If you'd like, I can propose a staged approach: small immediate top-up (prorated), then a commit uplift at the next billing cycle with a modest staged discount. That tends to reduce invoice shock.

I'm looping in Ben and Marissa from Sales to help with pricing and approval. I'll follow up with concrete numbers and a draft amendment for legal.

Quick Q: is Aurelia looking for a 12-month commitment on the new capacity or to align remaining term only?

— Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: FW: Mid-contract expansion: want to add capacity and co-term

FW: Elena from Aurelia (external) — they want to add ~200K dedicated units and co-term to their existing renewal date. Spec attached.

Ask: can you review the spec and propose: 1) two pricing options (annualize new capacity vs prorate immediate top-up), 2) recommended accelerator credit amount or percentage we can offer without manager approval, and 3) suggested rollout (canary / gradual ramp) so we can propose operational support and SLA adjustments.

Notes: They prefer minimal change to billing cadence if possible. Deal id DL-2026-783.

Thanks — Jasmine
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FW: Mid-contract expansion: want to add capacity and co-term

Jasmine — reviewed the spec. My preliminary pricing suggestion below (numbers illustrative; will confirm with finance ops):

Option A — Annualize new capacity (recommended for predictability):
- New 200K units annualized: list price $420k/year.
- We can offer a 12% uplift discount for a full 12-month commit if they agree to annualize to their renewal date and sign an amendment.
- Effective annualized spend: ~$369.6k.

Option B — Immediate prorated top-up (minimal change to billing):
- Pro-rata for remainder of term: ~$85k (based on 4 months remaining).
- No uplift discount for prorate, but offer a one-time accelerator credit of $10k applied to the first invoice to offset migration costs.

Hybrid (staged):
- Start with prorated top-up to cover immediate needs (Option B) + formalize an annualized uplift at next billing cycle at a 8% discount + $7k accelerator credit. This reduces invoice impact and keeps their team flexible.

Operational suggestion (Marissa feel free to comment):
- Canary pool for first 30 days (10% of capacity) with monitoring/ingress rules. After validation, scale to 100% over two billing cycles.

Approvals: I can approve up to 10% discount and $12k one-time credit. Anything above that needs manager sign-off. Legal will need to review the amendment; I recommend we produce Draft_Amendment_v1.docx and share for a quick redline.

— Ben
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Draft_Amendment_v1.docx (docx, 24KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FW: Mid-contract expansion: want to add capacity and co-term

Agree with Ben's hybrid approach — adds predictability without forcing cashflow pain. A few additions:
- Recommend a temporary 60% waiver on overage charges for the first 45 days after scale (gives Aurelia operational runway).
- Suggest we include a performance SLA addendum for the dedicated pool during the canary (baseline p99 target + escalation contact).
- If procurement pushes for a larger accelerator credit, we can trade on a shorter payment window (net45 -> net30) as a concession instead of increasing credits.

If we can keep total concession value under $20k, I can greenlight without exec escalation.

— Marissa
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@aurelia.ai>, procurement@aurelia.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mid-contract expansion: want to add capacity and co-term

Elena — thanks for your patience while we pulled this together. Below is our proposed package to support Aurelia's mid-contract uplift with minimal billing disruption. This is not final legal language but should be enough to move procurement.

Proposal (DL-2026-783):
- Immediate: prorated top-up for remainder of current term (~$86k) to cover the next 4 months (invoice in December).
- Next billing cycle: convert the uplift to an annualized 200K committed pool aligned to your existing renewal date. Annualized list: $420k; early-sign discount applied: 10% -> $378k effective.
- One-time accelerator credit: $10k applied to the December invoice to offset migration/ingress work.
- Overages: 60% waiver on overage fees for the first 45 days post-scale.
- Operational: 30-day canary (10% traffic) then scale to 100% over two billing cycles. We'll include a dedicated escalation contact and an SLA addendum for the dedicated pool during the canary period.
- Billing terms: standard net45. If procurement prefers a shorter payment term in lieu of increasing credits, we can discuss net30 as a trade.

Next steps:
1) If Aurelia is comfortable, I'll send the Draft Amendment (attached) for legal redline + a DocuSign powerform link to sign.
2) We'll schedule a short ops kick-off (30 min) to confirm canary controls and monitoring.

Please let me know by EOD Thursday if this looks acceptable and whether Aurelia prefers the net30 trade option.

Thanks — Jasmine
